page: Microsoft Azure L2s_v4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the Lsv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 2 threads, delivering 2 vCPUs. The processor includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and Intel AMX for matrix operations. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core, and includes 480 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capability. No GPUs are included in this configuration.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression rate of 31.24 GB/sec. However, because the instance is limited to a single physical core with hyper-threading, multi-core and parallelized workloads perform poorly. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated in the bottom 10% with a score of 1992.19, and the Geekbench multi-core score is in the bottom 25% at 2622.0. Memory bandwidth is also a bottleneck, with large-block read and write speeds falling into the bottom 10% at 20.23 GB/sec and 14.38 GB/sec respectively.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the L2s_v4 offers a high local storage-to-vCPU ratio and a generous 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, making it a viable entry-point option for storage-heavy or memory-leaning workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. However, the low multi-core performance and restricted memory bandwidth present significant tradeoffs for compute-intensive tasks. This instance is best suited for lightweight database operations, basic text processing, single-threaded file compression, or low-concurrency web serving where local storage capacity is prioritized over raw multi-threaded throughput.

It features 16.0 GB of RAM, a 260 MB L3 cache, and 480 GB of Premium Storage-capable local storage. While single-core performance is strong—highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2138.0 and a gzip compression speed of 31.24 GB/sec—multi-core performance and memory bandwidth are limited, with stress-ng multi-core and large-block memory writes scoring in the bottom 10%. This resource profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-efficient for storage-centric workloads with low parallel processing demands.
